exclude: The file as it was loaded, before it unpacks: the BASIC line SYS 2064, the decruncher's start at $0810 (it moves the packed data to $EC00-$FFFF and its own 256-byte loop from $0848 to $0100, then jumps there), and the packed data itself, left behind once it is moved. Not annotated, as the kit does with loaders and unpackers; the decruncher's output begins at $17FF with a zero that nothing reads, and the program is $1800-$3F98.
The packed data, moved here by the decruncher's start and read back from here as it unpacks downward into $17FF-$3F98: what is left once the program runs, under the KERNAL ROM.

comments.text: The picture's colour RAM: 1000 bytes, one for each 8x8 cell, row by row from the top left, whose low four bits give the colour of the cell's %11 pixels (the high four bits are ignored: colour RAM keeps only four). picture_show copies the four pages to $D800-$DBFF, so the 24 bytes $1BE8-$1BFF past the last cell go with them and are never shown.
picture_colour's second page, cells 256-511 (rows 6-12 from the 16th cell of row 6): copied to $D900 in picture_show's loop.
picture_colour's third page, cells 512-767 (rows 12-19 from the 32nd cell of row 12): copied to $DA00.
picture_colour's last page, cells 768-999 (rows 19-24 from the 8th cell of row 19) and the 24 bytes past them: copied to $DB00.

The picture's screen matrix: 1000 bytes, one for each 8x8 cell, whose high four bits colour the cell's %01 pixels and low four bits its %10 pixels; most cells are $0C, black for %01 and mid grey for %10. picture_show copies the four pages to $0400-$07FF, so the 24 bytes $1FE8-$1FFF past the last cell land on the sprite pointers, with every sprite off.
picture_screen's second page, cells 256-511: copied to $0500.
picture_screen's third page, cells 512-767: copied to $0600.
picture_screen's last page, cells 768-999 and the 24 bytes past them: copied to $0700, the last 24 onto the sprite pointers.

The picture's bitmap, multicolour, 320 bytes to each row of 40 cells and 8 bytes to a cell, two bits to a pixel (%00 the background colour, light grey). Rows 0-2: the panel's rounded top corners in black against the black border, and the top of the two hairs on Clyde's head.
Bitmap rows 3-5: the hairs and the brown top of Clyde's head; on the right the top of CLYDE in red, orange, yellow, green and blue letters with black shadows.
Bitmap rows 6-8: Clyde's big yellow eyes with black pupils, ringed in black, the pink of his face beginning, and the rest of CLYDE.
Bitmap rows 9-11: the green hand with which Clyde points at the player, on the left; NEEDS in blue, green, yellow, orange and red.
Bitmap rows 12-14: Clyde's yellow face and black mouth, the hand's lower fingers, and YOUR in large white letters.
Bitmap rows 15-17: Clyde's pink belly shaded in dithered grey, with his navel, the bottom of YOUR and the top of HELP!.
Bitmap rows 18-20: Clyde's green feet, and HELP! in red, orange, yellow, green and light green.
Bitmap rows 21-23: the black line under Clyde's feet, the plain light grey of the panel, and the top of a signature at the bottom right.
Bitmap row 24, the last: the panel's rounded bottom corners, the rest of the signature, in two greys, and on the bottom pixel line a stripe of green and one of light blue.

The program the decruncher runs (the file's BASIC line is SYS 2064, $0810, the decruncher's start): with interrupts off it blanks the screen ($D011 = 0), silences the SID ($D418), turns the sprites off and makes the border black, then copies picture_colour to colour RAM and picture_screen to the screen at $0400, 256 bytes of each page in one loop.

Turns the picture on: bitmap mode with the screen visible ($D011 = $3B), multicolour with 40 columns ($D016 = $D8), a light grey background ($D021 = $0F) and the bitmap at $2000 with the screen at $0400 ($D018 = $18).
Jumps to itself for ever, with interrupts still off: the picture stays until the machine is reset.
